case.title: Ford's links to BTR
case.subtitle: BTR Mediterranean Anode · Tangier, Morocco; Ford and BlueOval SK, USA
case.question: Can Sayari and open sources show a commercial link between Ford, or its battery joint venture BlueOval SK, and BTR's Chinese-owned plants?
case.answer: Yes, but not through Morocco yet. In 2026, BTR's Indonesian plant shipped artificial graphite to Ford's own battery plant in Michigan. In 2025, BTR's Chinese sales company shipped graphite to BlueOval SK. The Moroccan link is still only a contract: a US$120m Ford prepayment named in a Chinese filing, with no shipments so far.
case.why_it_matters: Under the PFE rules, Ford's battery tax credits depend on who owns its suppliers. BTR owns all three supply routes found here: China, Indonesia and Morocco. Ford's prepayment ties it to the Moroccan plant before that plant has produced anything.
case.headline: A Chinese filing says Ford agreed to prepay US$120m to BTR's Tangier anode company, but Tangier has shipped nothing yet. Meanwhile, US import data show BTR graphite already reaching Ford: about 960 t from BTR Indonesia at Ford's Marshall, Michigan plant in 2026, and 28 rows from BTR's Shenzhen sales arm at BlueOval SK in 2025.
case.summary_for_non_experts: BTR is a Chinese company that makes graphite for battery anodes, the negative side of a battery cell. In 2024, the company that holds the largest stake in BTR said Ford would pay BTR's new Moroccan plant US$120m in advance for future graphite. We couldn't find Ford confirming this, and the Moroccan plant hasn't exported anything yet. But customs records show BTR graphite already going to a Ford-owned battery plant in Michigan from BTR's Indonesian factory, and to Ford's joint venture with SK On from BTR in China.

steps.title: The deal: a prepayment on paper
steps.text: On 13 Aug 2024, BTR announced a 60,000-tonne anode plant in Tangier, through its subsidiary 'BTR Mediterranean Anode'. The same day, China Baoan, BTR's largest shareholder, said that subsidiary would sign supply and prepayment agreements with Ford, with Ford paying US$120m in advance for artificial graphite. Two later secondary sources say US$108m has been paid, but they give different dates. We found no Ford statement, and BTR's 2026 half-year report timed out when we tried to read it.

steps.title: Which Moroccan company? The filing points to the second one
steps.text: BTR has two Tangier companies. The filing's name, 'BTR Mediterranean Anode', matches the one registered in May 2024 (RC 149725). Moroccan company data show it is 100% owned by Rian International Holding in Singapore, and Case 2 traced that company to BTR. Case 2 had treated the other company, owned via BNUO and BTR (Jiangsu), as the anode subsidiary. That one is more likely the cathode project. Both are BTR-owned, so the ownership answer is the same.

steps.title: Morocco: graphite in, nothing out
steps.text: The Tangier anode company received its first BTR Indonesia graphite in Aug 2026 (Case 2). Sayari shows no exports from either Moroccan company. The graph tools couldn't test a path from Ford or BlueOval SK to Tangier: both searches timed out. For now, the Ford link to Morocco exists only in filings.

steps.title: Indonesia: BTR graphite at Ford's own plant
steps.text: From May to Sep 2026, US import data show 9 rows of artificial graphite (HS 3801.10, about 960 t gross) from PT Indonesia BTR to Ford's LFP cell plant in Marshall, Michigan, plus 2 rows to a second record for the same plant. Press says Ford wholly owns this plant, outside the SK On venture. Six of the 9 rows were loaded at Ningbo or Yantian in China, under the Indonesian company's name and Kendal address. A port of loading isn't proof of origin, but it warrants due diligence. BTR Indonesia had already shipped to SK Battery America in Aug 2025 (Case 1).

steps.title: China: BTR's sales arm supplies BlueOval SK
steps.text: BlueOval SK's supplier list in Sayari includes three BTR records. BTR's Shenzhen sales company sent 28 rows to BlueOval SK from Jan to Nov 2025, mostly described as 'graphite', some with purchase-order numbers. A BTR (Jiangsu) record sent one row of cathode material in Mar 2025. That is the same BTR subsidiary that owns BTR's first Moroccan company. Sayari also lists SK Battery America, which buys from BTR, as BlueOval SK's manager.

steps.title: What a buyer can't see
steps.text: Most of BlueOval SK's graphite (45 rows in 2025) is filed under Chinese freight forwarders, Pactra Tianjin and Fan Cheng, so the maker is hidden. Sayari shows no owners for BlueOval SK and nothing under 'Ford Motor' for HS 3801. Ford's imports sit on plant-name records that don't link to Ford. BlueOval SK also re-exported 'anode active material' to SK On Hungary in 2026, so where BTR material ends up can't be traced.

caveats: Buying graphite from BTR, or prepaying a supplier, is legal and common. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by Ford, BlueOval SK, SK On or BTR.
The US$120m figure comes from a listed company's filing as reported by Chinese media. The US$108m paid figure comes from secondary sources that disagree on the date, and is unverified.
A port of loading (Ningbo, Yantian, Singapore) is not a country of origin. The Chinese-port rows may reflect routing, not where the graphite was made.
Ford's ownership of the Marshall plant and its stake in BlueOval SK come from the press and the case brief, not from Sayari's registry data.
We read 100 of 653 BTR sales-arm rows into the US and 50 of 97 BTR Indonesia rows, so counts are minimums.
BTR's stock code on the Beijing Stock Exchange appears as 835185 in 2024 filings and 920185 in 2026.
This case looks only for BTR links. A general scan of Ford's suppliers is a separate piece of work.
Records checked on 18 Oct 2026. Sayari merges and retires IDs, and several calls timed out (HTTP 408).

calls.question: What does the press say about a Ford supply deal with BTR's Tangier plant?
calls.result_summary: Yicai Global (14 Aug 2024), Electrive, Yabiladi and Battery-Tech all report that BTR's largest shareholder, China Boan (Baoan) Group, said the Moroccan anode project company would sign supply and prepayment deals with Ford, with a US$120m prepayment. BTR's own notice named no customer. A LinkedIn post says Ford has prepaid US$120m.
calls.interpretation: The deal is reported widely, but every report traces back to one Chinese filing. No Ford statement appears.

calls.result_summary: BTR's 13 Aug 2024 notice (Sina mirror and BTR website): a 60,000 t/yr anode project at Tangier Tech City through wholly owned subsidiary 'BTR Mediterranean Anode New Material Technology' (贝特瑞地中海负极), up to CNY 2.618bn, about 2 years to build; no customer named. Jiemian and Eastmoney summaries of China Baoan's same-day notice: that subsidiary plans to sign supply and prepayment agreements with Ford Motor and/or related companies to supply artificial graphite, with Ford prepaying US$120m, and a guarantee letter. A Sep 2026 article (52hrtt) says US$108m had been paid by end-Jun 2026. A Kaiyuan Securities report (Jul 2024) says BTR's Hong Kong arm holds 60% of the Indonesian plant.
calls.interpretation: The counterparty named in the filing is 'BTR Mediterranean Anode', which matches Moroccan registry record RC 149725, not the BNUO-owned company Case 2 labelled as the anode subsidiary.
